slot.brief: In a double-slit experiment a stated path difference (as a fraction of wavelength) exists at a point; convert to phase difference and find the intensity as a fraction of the maximum.

stem: In a double-slit experiment with equal-intensity slits, the path difference at a point is $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$. What is the intensity there as a fraction of the maximum intensity?

verdicts.working: The phase difference is $2\pi(\lambda/3)/\lambda=2\pi/3$. For equal-intensity slits, $I/I_{\max}=\cos^2(\Delta\phi/2)=\cos^2(\pi/3)=1/4$.

working:
$\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$; $\dfrac{I}{I_{\max}}=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Independent check: The phase difference is $2\pi(\lambda/3)/\lambda=2\pi/3$. For equal-intensity slits, $I/I_{\max}=\cos^2(\Delta\phi/2)=\cos^2(\pi/3)=1/4$.
solution:
The phase difference is $\phi=\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$. For equal-intensity slits,
$$\dfrac{I}{I_{\max}}=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)=\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{1}{4}.$$
